utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Registrar, kindly call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honour. This is case number IT-03-67-PT, the Prosecutor versus Vojislav Seselj.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Today is Tuesday, the 22nd of May, 2007. My greetings to all the people in the courtroom, to the OTP representatives. Good afternoon, Mr. Seselj. And good afternoon to all the people helping us in this hearing. We have a Status Conference today, and I would like to tell you, Mr. Seselj, that the next Status Conference will be held on Tuesday, 5th of June, at 9.00 a.m., next Status Conference, it will take place on Tuesday, the 5th of June, at 9.00 a.m., in this very courtroom. The agenda today, we have a series of questions I'd like to deal with one by one. First of all, I would like to inform you, Mr. Seselj, that regarding your motion whereby you wanted to be close to the Judges and the Prosecution or close to the witness when they come to testify, the registry has told me that they saw no inconvenience to Mr. Seselj being seated more to the front, but it will have to be in the second row. So you see, the bench that is behind the first one. This can be implemented as of the next Status Conference. This will make it possible for Mr. Seselj to have in front of him, if he so wishes, only his assistants who will be in front of him, behind the first bench, and he will be behind them. Personally, I would have preferred for him to be seated at the first bench, but the registry, for security reasons, has told me that that was not possible. So this is a compromise we arrived at, which is to place Mr. Seselj in the second row, so he will be much closer. Because I can see that in Courtroom I the accused is seated very far from the Bench, whilst in the other two courtrooms, the accused are -- is or are much closer which is much better, since we have the principle of equality of arms there's no reason for the Prosecutor to be closer to the Judges than the accused are. I was told by the registry that the accused in this case will be seated in the second row. This was the first thing. Second thing, Mr. Seselj, it has to do with the motion you filed for contempt to the Court and it concerned Ms. Carla del Ponte and her two deputies or lawyers in this case. You may know it, you may not. The Trial Chamber presided over by Judge Robinson with Judge Bonomy and myself issued a decision on the 15th of May. It is, no doubt, being translated so you may not have had it in your own language, but I'm going to explain to you what the content is. The Trial Chamber unanimously deemed that it was proper to settle this issue at the end of the trial because the proceeding in question will make it possible for you as an accused to raise questions of all the witnesses that are to testify, be they Prosecution or Defence witnesses. Therefore, the witnesses will be under oath, and you will be able to ask them in which conditions their testimony was gathered. And this will have much stronger weight because the witnesses answering your questions will be under oath, as I said. Also, there is another advantage to these proceedings. If it turned out that a witness, especially so for the Prosecution witnesses, if it turned out that they had provided written statements under some kind of duress, pursuant to the Rules you would be entitled to ask for their testimony to be stricken, as part of the proceedings in place to gather testimony when witnesses are under oath. Therefore, the Trial Chamber presided over by Judge Robinson decided that it was proper not to dismiss your motion but to follow the issue very closely, enabling you yourself in person to question witnesses who may have been involved in reproach as you mentioned in your submissions. And only in fine, when all the witnesses have testified will be you be entitled to renew your submissions and the Trial Chamber will then rule having all the relevant material in possession. So this is a decision that was issued recently. You will receive it in your own language if you haven't yet received it. So at this juncture do you have anything to say on this issue; if so, you have the floor.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Judge, I have a few things to say with regard to this matter. As for this decision of the Trial Chamber, I haven't seen it yet; however, some of the media in Belgrade already provided brief information about that kind of a decision. In a way, I have been informed beforehand, and I am going to file a motion to appeal for several reasons. First of all, these are two separate crimes. The crime that I have been charged with and the other crime that I am charging the Chief Prosecutor Carla del Ponte with and two of her co-workers. They cannot be tried together with me. The proceedings against them may or may not take place, but there certainly cannot be a joinder of our two trials because otherwise the three of them would have to sit next to me as defendants, and I'm sure you're going to avoid that at all costs. Secondly, Carla del Ponte is leaving this Tribunal in the month of September. No one is going to catch her anymore and bring her before this court to try her for contempt. Once my trial is over - that's going to be towards the end of 1998 - rather, the year is 2008, then it will only be the Trial Chamber that will be operative but there will be no more first-instance trials. So postponing the contempt hearing is a deft manoeuvre to free potential perpetrators of all responsibility. I did not file these charges to make things easier for myself, but rather I want to brand these terrible crimes, I'm talking about Carla del Ponte and her co-workers and what they did are far greater crimes than the crimes I'm being charged with. The practice to date of the Trial Chambers within this Tribunal in terms of contempt was different, but at any rate when there was a case of contempt of court, Trial Chambers would stop proceedings against the accused person concerned and then they would immediately move on to contempt hearings regarding various individuals, sometimes Defence counsel, sometimes witnesses. For example, we remember the lawyer Vujin from the Tadic case as far as I can remember. Then also the attempt to charge the Blaskic lawyer and so on, and then Kosta Bulatovic, a witness in the Milosevic case who didn't want to answer questions put by the Prosecution because the accused was not present at the hearing because of illness and he did not want to take part in proceedings that were held in the absence of the accused on account of his illness. Also, there were cases when persons who were charged with disclosing secrets, or rather, protected documents appeared. For example, certain journalists from Croatia who were charged with disclosing the name of their president, Stipe Mesic, as a protected witness in the Blaskic case. I'm saying this in open court now because the protective measures are no longer in force, all of this is well-known now, and the judgements are not under embargo, they are public as well. So there was never any hesitancy in terms of bringing criminal charges here, however in my particular case, I draw the following conclusion: The Trial Chamber realises that my arguments are very strong and well founded on the basis of the arguments that I presented in respect of Carla del Ponte and her co-workers. They may be sentenced to up to seven years in prison. Yesterday, I filed an addendum to my motion with 14 new statements of persons who were heard by investigators from The Hague and who were blackmailed by the investigators and made to give false testimony, to perjure themselves. Among them is the wife, or rather, widow of Milan Babic. As you know, Milan Babic, because he was fed up with giving false testimony in other trials, he committed suicide during the Martic trial. The wife of Milan Babic wrote about all the pressures that he and she and their entire family lived under. The entire family was basically under arrest, not formally but that is the way they were actually treated. Also I have the statement of Zoran Mijatovic, the former deputy of the head of the State Security Service of service. He testifies, or rather, he gives a statement saying that investigators from The Hague Tribunal were trying to force him to artificially link me up with the Yellow Wasps, so that I would be proven to be an accomplice in the Zvornik war crimes. Also there is a series of others. The members of my legal team are still working on this matter, they are still collecting statements from persons who are now reporting about this themselves. Before we were searching for such people but now they are coming to us of their own free will and telling us what kind of pressure was brought to bear on them or how they were threatened or how their services were even attempted to be bought in such cases. So I absolutely do not agree to have any kind of deferral of proceedings with regard to this matter; the Trial Chamber has to accept these proceedings or refuse to conduct proceedings if they believe that there aren't sufficient arguments for this. Since there's an abundance of arguments here, I think it is impossible for the Trial Chamber to rule that my motion should be repealed, and the Trial Chamber wanted to avoid bringing criminal charges against Carla del Ponte towards the end of her career. So those are incontrovertible facts. Now what is sought is a compromise. There will be proceedings but only after my trial is over. No, the proceedings cannot take place then because if my trial starts only in November, it will certainly last until the last days of 2008. It cannot be over before that. The Prosecution needs six months, there has to be a three-month break, and I need at least six months. Judge, what you said is that I will have the right to ask for statements that were made under duress to be stricken from the record; however, that is my not intention. The criminal charges I filed were supported by these statements and by those included in the addendum from yesterday. They're not going to be Prosecution witnesses at all. I am going to cross-examine Prosecution witnesses and prove in that way that they were lying and show how they were pressured and blackmailed. I would like to remind you of the Slobodan Milosevic case. During the trial, in the case of over 40 witnesses, he convinced the Trial Chamber that the witnesses did not know what was in their 92 bis statement submitted by the Prosecution. Mr. Milosevic had the right to cross-examine these witnesses, and he said, You said such and such a thing, and then the witness said, I have no idea, I never said that, somebody else, I don't know, maybe there's a mistake in the interpretation or the translation, and so on and so forth. There were over 40 such cases. Now this Rule 92 bis is subdivided further, but in essence it remains the same. I think that it will only happen in the future when we see how people were mistreated and how they were coerced into perjuring themselves and giving false testimony against me. Maybe these people that I am referring to, whose statements I collected will come to the courtroom if I call them as witnesses but you are restricting my time in advance. You are making me call certain witnesses, or rather, these witnesses rather than other ones that I want to call. So I am spending my time and my resources and so on and so forth. These witnesses should be called by the Court during the contempt proceedings against Carla del Ponte and her co-workers. The only right way of resolving this would be for the Trial Chamber to set up an independent investigating body or appoint an independent prosecutor, who would then hear all the persons who are mentioned in the criminal report, and who would also hear all the investigators whose names are mentioned in this negative context as persons who resorted to blackmail, pressure, and bribery. Then the said person would either file an indictment on the basis of that or report the whole situation to the Court. In these proceedings I can only be sitting on the sidelines as an interested party. In such proceedings, I would not be the prosecuting or the defending party. I just want to hear this because what happened happened in the investigation procedure of my trial. The independent prosecutor should be here and your Trial Chamber should judge that. That is the only right way to proceed. Secondly, an argument I did not hear from you but that was mentioned in the Belgrade press; namely, that my trial is running too late, so that is why you want to leave these proceedings until after my trial is over. But that is not based on any relevant arguments either. At the last Status Conference, the Prosecutor stated that they will be ready in November to start the trial. Judging by the way things were going so far, it depends whether they will be able to begin in November, so that is in another six months' time and during those six months the Trial Chamber has enough time to act on these charges that I brought, to investigate the facts, to check them out, and to pass a relevant decision. There is no reason to wait, especially because there is the possibility of the accused parties running away, escaping. Carla del Ponte leaves in September --

utterances.speaker: MS. DAHL
utterances.text: Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Switzerland does not have the obligation to hand over its own citizens to this Tribunal. Switzerland is not a member of the UN, and therefore -- Ms. Dahl, please do not interrupt me. I never interrupted you. I never offended you in any way. Please allow me to finish.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] One moment, Ms. Dahl, you will have the floor. Let him finish because he's setting forth his reasons and you can respond to what he said --

utterances.speaker: MS. DAHL
utterances.text: The parties' filings are confidential and I move that this session be closed during the discussions of the material that has been filed before the Trial Chamber confidentially. The order is not confidential; however, the submissions of the parties are. The practice direction concerning the contempt proceedings requires that prior to an investigation and prior to a decision that all the material remain confidential.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm going to answer you in a minute, but I'll let Mr. Seselj finish. Please finish, Mr. Seselj.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This cannot be confidential, because I filed these charges publicly and it was published in 10.000 copies in my book, "Either Carla's Witness or Death". All these 10.000 copies were sold out in Serbia and very soon an English edition is going to be published. Also, a scientific gathering was held in Belgrade devoted to this subject. Over 6.000 people were there, and prominent Serbian lawyers presented their views on the matter. And also, the addendum is also a public document and has already been distributed to the media. Not a single one of my arguments can be a secret because I didn't want anything to be a secret. Possibly your answer is going to be a secret, and I am going to honour that if you say officially that it's a secret document, that it's an official secret. But you, making my documents secret, no way. I decided that this is going to be public, I published this, it came out in this book, it came out in the newspaper Velika Srbija, and this was carried practically by all the daily newspapers in Serbia. These persons who you blackmailed to give false testimony went to various Belgrade newspapers for days and then they explained extensively how you treated them. Some of them, like Jovo Ostojic, wrote their own books about their own experience. How can that possibly be a secret? Of course, if you conduct secret proceedings you have reasons for this secrecy. You want to hide some of your own secrets. Such proceedings can be secret; however, as I wrote as a motion, as criminal charges, will never be secret because I would not allow such a thing to be secret. You used to behave that way in some other cases, but you cannot behave that way in my case because there is just this one power, one strength I have and that is the power of the public and nothing more than that. And it is that power of the public that made it impossible for you to bury me a long time ago. You have already buried many others who did not resort to the public; Milan Babic, Deronjic, who died on Friday, if I'm not mistaken, and others. All these people who you instrumentalised to give false testimonies, they committed suicide. One of them committed suicide, he was supposed to be a false witness in my case and he committed suicide sometime this summer. I am not going to mention his name because there is still an embargo on his name, although the Prosecutor did ask for the secrecy to be removed and I don't know whether the Trial Chamber has ruled until now. So you forced one of them to get bad cancer that simply devoured him, the other one hanged himself. So this is what happens with your false witnesses and it is high time for someone to investigate that matter as well. I have given instructions to my legal advisors to talk to the attorneys and family of Miroslav Deronjic to say what kind of pressure was exerted on him. Bratunac is not in my indictment, but when they arrested him, they beat him up. They put him into a barrel of water and so on and so forth. They threatened him here, blackmailed him, threatened him with a life sentence and he gave false testimony in one, two, three trials and all of it added up. You think the public is never going to find out about all of that? Oh yes, they will. I will do my best that they find out and they are going to find out, and you cannot keep such things secret. What your crimes are cannot be kept secret.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: The speaker is speaking much too fast.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Seselj, I have various things to say following your questions and what you said. With regard to confidentiality - and I'm addressing the Prosecutor as well - Rule 77 regarding contempt says nowhere that the proceedings should remain confidential. Therefore, the accused in his submissions is entitled to state publicly or orally what he feels he has to say. So your arguments as to the fact that the proceedings under Rule 77 should be confidential, I can't see that, either in the Rules or in the Statute. You could shed some light on this; I'm all ears.

utterances.speaker: MS. DAHL
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would refer the Court's attention, respectfully, to the Practice Direction issued by the Registrar on 6 May 2004 concerning the investigation and prosecution of contempt before the International Tribunal. Paragraph 5 of the Practice Direction provides: "The request for an investigation shall be made ex parte and confidentially before the Chamber in which the contempt allegedly occurred." I have the cover sheet of the filing of Mr. Seselj's motion. It is stamped "confidential," as was the Prosecution's response in direction -- in response to the direction of the Trial Chamber. The cascade of criminal accusations of wrongdoing, of belligerence and intimidation by witnesses are denied by the Prosecution without any qualification, and we should not be made to listen where there is no proceeding pending to adjudicate those facts. Respectfully, Your Honour, this needs to be in closed session to protect the privacy of the people who have been accused from malicious and slanderous accusations that are false and are without any basis in fact. This office does not, has not, and will never bribe, intimidate, coerce, or otherwise seek to improperly influence the testimony of witnesses. Our task is to do justice, and the foundation of that is the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Regarding the Practice Direction by the Registrar, I am only bound by the Rules of Procedure and Evidence, and I remind you that in the Rules there are provisions for the President to issue practice directions. This is Rule 19(B) of the Rules. I'm going to read it out because it is relevant. "The President may from time to time, and in consultation with the Bureau, the Registrar and the Prosecutor, issue Practice Directions, consistent with the Statute and the Rules, addressing detailed aspects of the conduct of proceedings before the Tribunal." But such practice directions as they are issued must be consistent with the Rules. The Rules governing contempt proceedings are to be found in Rule 77 and nothing in Rule 77 says that everything has to happen secretly. So on this issue I have a very clear view, there is no place for secrecy in this matter. Now, let me answer Mr. Seselj. Firstly, you pointed out that you had sent us a new list with 14 witnesses. I've just learned it, just as you said so. The Legal Officer of the Trial Chamber immediately told me that you had sent 180 pages in Cyrillic on this issue, and the pages are being translated. This new addendum of yours has not yet been registered with the registry, which accounts for the fact that I was not informed of this. Of course, clearly, this is information that the Trial Chamber could take into account if it were to review the decision it issued on the 15th of May. All the more so, since you told us that among the 15 new witnesses there would be the widow of Mr. Babic, who allegedly mentioned she had been put under pressure, if I properly understood what you said. We issued this decision on the 15th of May. You are still free to file another motion for a review of the said motion and decision, asking us to review our decision, since now you are providing, according to what you said, new information through this addendum. This being said, but you know the proceedings as well as I do, you could also ask for appeal certification, and I can tell you straight ahead that I would be more than willing to grant it. But regardless, from this you conveyed several other pieces of information which would make us believe that the proceedings -- that you believe that the proceedings cannot take place. Let me answer your arguments. It is true to say that all things being equal, further to a decision of the Security Council, first-instance trials should be finished by 2008. And as for the Appeals Chamber, it would -- the deadline would be 2010. But there may be situations in which trials would go on beyond 2008, and anything that is parallel proceedings will proceed as well. So you seem to be showing some concern about this, but I can already provide you with an answer which is nearly certain, I mean, we're not going to stop everything overnight in 2009 saying, Now we stop working altogether, and especially because the trials will not be over by then. And then you submitted that since the person in question will no longer be working in this Tribunal, he or she cannot be prosecuted. You're wrong there again, because as you know when it comes to contempt proceedings, the Chamber seized of such proceedings has various means at its disposal. And you know very well that there were contempt proceedings in which the Trial Chamber delivered warrants of arrest to the people, no matter where they lived. So you don't need to have any concern on this. As to the merits on the proceedings, Rule 77 provides the following proceeding. Regarding the investigation, because that seemed to be sort of nagging you, it is either the Prosecutor that carries out the investigation; in this instance it would be impossible, the Prosecutor cannot investigate him or herself. So this possibility is ruled out. The other procedural option that can be envisaged and that I, myself, envisaged, was to have an amicus curiae appointed. He would be in charge of conducting the investigation. And you seem to be sort of pointing to that type of proceeding. You seem to be suggesting this to the Trial Chamber. So if you have an amicus curiae, the person appointed is fully independent. His or her timetable is defined by the person him or herself. They will do what they think necessary. Therefore, this type of proceedings may present advantages but also inconvenience. The other possibility would be for the Trial Chamber itself to carry out the investigation, but in this case also there would be a problem because the Trial Chamber cannot be Judge and party because they would have to examine the OTP witnesses, witnesses in court or out of court. So that's a problem, too. So on the basis of all these factors, we chose an avenue which safeguards your rights, because indeed when a witness comes to testify, let's say a Prosecution witness whom you think pressure was bought to bear on them, you can ask questions of that person who is under oath. And if the witness failed to come because they would not be a Prosecution witness, you -- when you adduce your evidence in your case, you can call them. They can come, and they can testify under oath. And you will be the one conducting the examination-in-chief. Just think it over. Take all this on board. Nothing prevents you from filing new submissions for review over the decision we issued, taking into account that there are 14 new witnesses who've just appeared and whom I didn't know anything about, and I haven't had an opportunity yet to read your submissions but I shall certainly do so as soon as they have been translated. So, so much for this issue, but I'm sure we'll have another opportunity to deal with this again. Now, let me deal with what I see as major obstacles, hindrances, but they could -- they may not be or they have not yet been solved. Unless you want to take the floor, Ms. Dahl.

utterances.speaker: MS. DAHL
utterances.text: Very briefly, Your Honour. I would ask that you direct the Registrar to provide us with copies of the 14 new statements in their form now while we await translation. I think that would make our review of the witness statements more efficient. And I would note that under the Rules, a motion to certify for appellate review by the Prosecution would be due today and I'd respectfully request the Trial Chamber to enlarge that period by at least ten days until Friday, June 1st, so that we can complete our review of the witness statements and take the matter under further consideration in view of the comments you've offered today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Fine. You have that extension of deadline. Now, let's go back to disclosure under Rule 66 and 68, disclosure with hard copies. Mr. Seselj, you wrote submissions and your motion has been filed; Prosecution has 14 days to answer. So regarding the motion for disclosure in hard copy in your own language of the documents, I'm now asking Prosecution to make haste because as soon as I have these submissions the Chamber will rule on this. However -- yes, Ms. Dahl.

utterances.speaker: MS. DAHL
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I'm finding myself at a loss with regard to the specific motion that Your Honour is referring to because I am presently unaware of a motion regarding delivery of hard copies.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. The assistant told me that this was recorded -- registered on May 17th. If the mail office is working correctly, I'm sure that you have the submission from Mr. Seselj. I have them myself. It's May 17th.

utterances.speaker: MS. DAHL
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Fine, Mrs. Dahl. You have to stay on top of all these motions, there's many of them coming in. It's sometimes hard to find your way out, and personally 24 hours, around-the-clock, I'm, you know, checking this case to try and keep abreast of things and to make sure that some motions don't fall through and to make sure that I can answer all them. That regarding the issue of electronic -- of disclosure, whether it should be electronic or not, I told you that I found it necessary for the accused to obtain hard copies of all the elements under Rule 66 and 68. And the decision I will make will of course be guided by the spirit which I believe should prevail. So that is one obstacle, one fundamental obstacle for the -- for this trial. Now, another obstacle that I will now mention is the issue of payment of Mr. Seselj's assistants. As I told you, Mr. Seselj, I'll be fully transparent with you. I'm doing everything I can to keep you abreast of everything happening. Since -- in realtime because I believe that you must be kept abreast of the advancement of the obstacles that are encountered, notably on this item regarding the payment. So I was with the registry. We had a new working meeting to try and find out how registry may eventually pay your assistants, pay them for their work as well as pay them for the expenses incurred; for example, housing expenses and so on. The position of the registry is the following: The registry is telling me that the Statute in Article 21(4)(b) did not provide for -- provide for legal aid for the lawyer and provided nothing when an accused wants to self-represent himself. And registry is also telling me that, after having analysed the situation and also because of the fact that they are working in -- within budget limits, they cannot pay out anything. This position has always been expressed and was expressed quite some time ago, and I asked them to get information from the legal advisor in New York. And they did this and gave me a copy of a letter dated May 10th, 2007, letter sent to New York regarding this problem. As of now, we have not received any answer to this letter. But this is a very important question. As you know, at your own level you already contested the decision made by registry, you appealed to the President of the Tribunal, who actually said that registry was right, but telling you also that you had to seize the Chamber of this problem. I thought that I could settle this problem quickly; however, today I note that today, May 22nd, the problem is still pending. So you should quickly submit a motion to the Trial Chamber so that the Trial Chamber could rule on this. I'm -- I can tell you that as far as I'm concerned, personally, the way I interpret Article 21 of the Statute is as follows, and I believe that many people neglected this. Article 21(4) says the following, I will read it very slowly: "In the determination of any charge against the accused pursuant to the present Statute, the accused shall be entitled to the following minimum guarantees in full equality," and then the guarantees are spelled out. And what does this paragraph mean? Well, it means that the accused is entitled in full equality, full equality with Prosecution, to guarantees, and guarantees are, as I said, spelled out through (a), (b), (c), (d), (e), (f), and (g), through all those provisions; however, these are minimum guarantees that are provided for because the article says at least, "following minimum guarantees," which means there are initial guarantees that may be granted to the accused. But even if we only look at these minimum guarantees, the Statute provided for the possibility that an accused would self-represent himself or be aided by counsel. The Statute, thus, has provided for the fact that self-representation is possible and automatically this has consequences. Notably, since in these guarantees under (e), it is written that the accused may examine or have examined - and when you're saying "examined," it means he is examining, himself, the witnesses - and therefore Article 21, as I said earlier, provides the accused with a certain number of rights, including the right to self-representation, which of course entails a number of consequences. And among these consequences, you have the problem of collecting witnesses -- statements from witnesses, the cost incurred by expert witnesses, and so forth. I'm not going to go through the whole list, but this is important. Therefore, Mr. Seselj, you should very quickly draw up a motion regarding this, basing yourself on Article 21 of the Statute. The Appeals Chamber recognised that you had the right to self-representation, but this right that you have entails a number of consequences, notably your assistants and so on. Once the motion is written, Prosecution will have 14 days to reply to it, and I myself will rule on this, whatever the position taken by the registry. The registry announced and told me - and it's no surprise to you - that he also intends to get involved in the proceeding. You have made a motion, we'll have a reply from Prosecution, and registry will also intervene. But then a decision will be made. Maybe Prosecution will ask for a certification of appeal, the registry may also ask for the same thing. And in that case, it will be up to the Appeals Chamber to rule. As far as I'm concerned, I said - I said it already and I still state - that any accused has a right to self-representation and that this right, as provided for in the Statute, entails that the accused should have all the facilities required at his disposal to prepare his defence case. This is written in the Statute. So I wanted to mention this, given the -- this pending question, and I believe that this question can only be solved if maybe New York has in the meanwhile told registry that it can pay out and will have given the registry the order to pay out for the expenses and that would be the best solution possible. But if we hear nothing from New York, then the Trial Chamber or possibly the Appeals Chamber will have to live up to its responsibilities. And as far as I'm concerned, I'm ready to live up to my responsibility - I've always been ready to do so - and I will it do this as soon as I get the submissions from all parties. So do you want to take the floor, Mr. Seselj? Then I will give the floor to Mrs. Dahl.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Judge, I will continue to be adamant that the International Tribunal finance my defence. It is Article 21 of the Statute that provides me with this right, to be endowed with the means for my defence. In a couple of days I will be filing a motion to the Trial Chamber for the Trial Chamber to rule upon. Of course, should the International Tribunal end up not being involved in the financing of my defence that does not in itself mean that I will not defend myself; I will still defend myself but quite literally on my own. I will have to dismantle my team, I will have to release my legal advisors, and I will not be needing a case manager either. What would I keep one for? I will be entirely alone in the courtroom with no assistants, with no advisors, I will defend myself. It will be down to the Trial Chamber and the Tribunal as a whole to explain how such a trial can possibly be a just and equitable one. That is what I have decided. I will not accept any halfway house solutions. Secondly, it is quite symptomatic that the registrar is trying to hide certain information; how much money has been paid to the lawyers who were imposed to me so far. That is very symptomatic. Why should the registry refuse to disclose the cost of all the other defence cases in the financing of which the International Tribunal has been involved. Why is the registrar refusing to disclose how much money they have spent so far on my case, the investigators, administrative costs, and all the other expenses. This is UN money, and the way this money is used cannot be kept secret. Only those who were involved in murky business might want to keep this secret; they squandered the money or they laundered the money. I don't think that is too far off the mark either. These are symptomatic issues and that is what the whole thing rests upon. People from the registry have come to me several times to negotiate the financing of my defence. These negotiations were always disrupted when I placed the following condition: To know exactly how much the stand-by lawyers in my case cost, how much all the other defence cases cost them, and what the costs incurred by the OTP were. This is where it all stopped, after I raised that, and then they always say that I have no right to having my defence financed. I would have some if I dropped my three questions, but I want to ask those three questions and without those three questions being answered, nobody is in a position to say how much my defence case may cost. These are the only objective criteria that can be used to establish this. What we cannot have is them setting up new rules, setting up new criteria for this, which is entirely subjective. They might as well say: $100. All right, $100 but then prove that the OTP spent no more than $100, or that the International Tribunal awarded no more than $100 in other defence teams in previous trials. Or to prove that Aleksandar Lazarevic, Van der Spoel, and Hooper and everybody else, whoever, was nominated without my consent in my case would be awarded no more than $100. Just tell me that, prove me that. If they got no more, I can live with that, too. I will use up some of my own money and I will use the $100 that the International Tribunal will award me. That's what I'm saying. I'm just trying to put you in the picture to see how drastic this type of illegal behaviour can be.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I will give the floor to Mrs. Dahl in a minute but before so, Mr. Seselj, I have one more thing to add. While you were talking, I was checking Article 21 of the Statute again and we have the question of legal aid in Article 21 regarding an accused that would be no means, no financial means. So in this motion you will have to state exactly what -- what is your financial situation. I remember you told us that you had an account, bank account, in New York that was frozen; you have another account in Canada, but I think that great -- because of expenses incurred, most of the money is gone. And you also explained that you still had some resources, if I understood well, it was a pension or salary, I can't really remember, that was supposed to be paid out to you in Belgrade. Out of all this, I didn't realise that you had enough resources to pay out all these expenses incurred. So to make sure that the registry -- that the registry or Prosecution can test [Realtime transcript read in error "contest"] that you would not have sufficient means, I have of course no system to know exactly what your financial resources are, but in your motion you will have to tell us exactly what is your financial standing. If you have, for example, a certain amount of dollars that could help you pay out, the registry will say, Well, since he wants self-representation, that's his own choice and it's up to him now to pay his own assistants. So in the motion you have to give us all this information to make sure that the -- that the form of your motion is irreproachable and that it follows Article 21 and what is provided for in Article 21. But as I already told you -- I think I already told you this, you know, when I drew your attention on this problem of indigence. But you know case law inside-out, if I may say so, and I'm sure you know that some accused who had assigned counsel, well, for them the registry made a number of decisions to make sure that even though they had assigned counsel, they had to pay out from their own pockets some expenses because the registry took stock of the financial standing of the accused in that case. So with you, registry must know absolutely what your financial standing is in order to say that you could pay out so much money, with maybe 10 or 20 or 30 per cent of it being borne by you. I'm drawing your attention on this; in your motion you must be fully transparent on this issue. Mrs. Dahl, would you like to take the floor on this aspect of things regarding application of Article 21 in the Statute?

utterances.speaker: MS. DAHL
utterances.text: Not presently, Your Honour. I look forward to receiving Mr. Seselj's submissions. I would ask the court reporter to correct the transcript at page 23, line 19, where is the Court's statement was translated as "contest" and in fact the Court said "can test" to allow the Prosecutor and the registrar to test the submissions by Mr. Seselj.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Fine, fine. Very good. This will be settled. This is obviously -- something that is up to the registrar. Before the break now, I wish to deal with another problem.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Seselj, you have the floor.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I just wanted to say one thing, it is one sentence but perhaps a rather long one on the question of financing. Back in 2003, Judge, I submitted to the registrar all the relevant information. I filled in all the questionnaires. I did everything that I could and everything that was necessary. I will mention this again in my submission to the Trial Chamber. I now have a lot less money than I did back in 2003. I was never the one stalling this whole process, it was always the registry. Secondly, there is an obligation to provide legal assistance and this is linked to the presumption of innocence. I'm protected by the presumption of innocence, and it is the presumption of innocence, this very principle, that guarantees me the means for my defence. If I'm not awarded these means, that prejudices the very presumption of innocence and I am presumed to be guilty, to be a criminal deserving of no assistance whatsoever, whereas precisely that, Your Honour, is something that the OTP are yet to prove. The position of the registry being what it is, they would seem to imply that my guilt has already been proven; on the other hand, they're offering me their Defence counsel, their legal assistants. They're trying to infiltrate spies who will eventually end up undermining my defence as they have other people's, other accused's defences before this Tribunal. Once you have a counsel like that you can no longer get rid of him. When you have a Defence counsel, you as an accused, are reduced to the status of an idiot and you're not allowed to say a single word. That was the case with the Appeals Chamber saying that I would be allowed to address the Court only through my Defence counsel and not on my own. That is the very essence of these Kafkaesque proceedings before this Tribunal. Bring them here and do not allow them to defend themselves. We have had only two cases where the accused defended themselves. There were other cases where some of the accused threatened to defend themselves and then all of their requests and wishes were met in terms of who their appointed Defence counsel should be, just to keep them from representing themselves. That is the essence. Fortunately, I have recognised this essence of the problem in a timely manner. I studied all the other trials, all the other cases, and I have prepared myself for my own trial in a timely manner. That is why they have not succeeded in double-crossing me. That is why the OTP are now powerless. That is why they have no evidence against me, and without cooperation from a false Defence counsel, an imposed one, they are powerless to do anything against me at all. They are still expecting things to change. They still have not disclosed a lot of these documents to me in Serbian and in hard copy. It seems that they are just biding their time, waiting for something to finally happen.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Fine. I heard you well, and I'm now waiting for your submissions. I'm looking forward to them. So now before the break, I believe we should deal with another topic which is also extremely important in your case which is the date at which the trial should start. Last time you heard Mrs. Dahl say, for information, that as far as she was concerned the trial should not -- couldn't start before November. Since then, I've investigated the availability of courtrooms, I've investigated on the resources of registry to try and make sure that the trial could start as quickly as possible. I'm fully transparent, as I told you and I'm going to tell you exactly what the situation is regarding trials occurring now and trials to come. As you know, there are three courtrooms here. This is Courtroom I, there's also Courtroom II and Courtroom III. So regarding current trials, there's Milutinovic case, which is mainly occurring in Courtroom III, it is scheduled to end - of course this is subject to variations - but it is scheduled to end in mid-2008. After that, another trial might be scheduled. The other trial in Courtroom III, which I preside over, is the Prlic case. This trial will go on throughout 2007 and 2008, which means that Courtroom III is fully booked. So let's move to the other courtrooms. The Boskoski trial just started and is roughly scheduled to last over several months and might end early in 2008. And then another case is scheduled to take place in that courtroom right after that one. In Courtroom I, the Popovic et al. case is underway. Normally it is scheduled, through estimation -- it is estimated to be -- to end by 2009, in the first three months of 2009. Now, regarding Courtroom II, there's the Dragomir Milosevic trial going on, and this one should end in November of this year. So this would free up Courtroom II. The Haradinaj trial has also started and will probably continue into 2008. And then there's another case that is to be tried, the Delic trial, and this one is scheduled to run until mid-2008. So now if you look at the statistics, we see that we have 15 accused, including yourself, awaiting trial. I'm sure you know it because this is no secret, everybody is well aware of it, is that we still have six fugitives, Mr. Karadzic, Mr. Mladic, Mr. Zupljanin, Mr. Hadzic, Mr. Djordjevic, and Mr. Tolimir. And of course, if they're arrested they will come under trial. So when you look at the schedule of courtrooms and you -- and the only available slot that we have, which is at the end of the Milosevic trial, your case could be tried in November. Of course we have the problem of the courtroom on the one hand, but on the other hand we have another problem which is the resources that need to be mobilised. As you see in a courtroom you've got legal officers, registrars, a court -- court reporter, interpreters, OTP members, the SLOs, so we need -- all this staff is subjected to a budget, a specific budget, and the trial -- this Tribunal can run six trials at once, not seven. And in this -- we need, therefore, to have -- the one trial to be over to start a new one because of budgetary constraints. I've had many contacts with many people, and I am told that November could really be the most suitable date for your trial to start. I know, Mr. Seselj, that you have been detained for several years; I'm well aware of this. I'm well aware of the presumption of innocence also. I know that your trial had started, but for procedural -- for procedural issue regarding the rights of the defence, your trial had to be postponed and it came back to pre-trial stage. So this is the data I have at my disposal and I believe that you must be told about all this information. I don't want to use administrative reasons to hide; I just want you to know what the situation is in full transparency. Now, independently of all of this, of all that I've said, I'm sure that you must understand and that Prosecution must understand that as of now there's still documents that you have not received in our own language that you will have to study in order to defend yourself. And secondly, there's also a pending question, the question of your assistants. Earlier you said that eventually, possibly, you could even defend yourself on your own, but that would not be a fair trial. And I can't say I don't share your opinion, because, you know, in a cell with this procedure I really don't see how you can defend yourself alone; technically, I think it's absolutely impossible. Furthermore, there is a great number of motions - we'll see them later - which are calling for replies, either by you or by your counsel or your advisors. And if you want to be in the best condition possible to defend yourself - and what are these conditions exactly, in the best condition possible? Being in your situation, defending yourself, cross-examining witnesses, directing the proceeding, developing your strategy, investigating, himself, in order to find witnesses, being able also to interview the witnesses and so on. Well, this is going to require great effort from you, and I believe that this is a huge task if you want to go at it alone. I'm sure you need help. I know that you need help. Let me give you an example so you fully understand the magnitude of the effort required. There are several motions regarding expert witnesses. An admission of an expert report has been requested. So an expert report requires the accused and the counsel, if there is one, but of course, you are -- you are your own lawyer, so you have to read and study the expert report. Sometimes it's several hundred pages long. You have to look at all the footnotes also in the expert report in order to prepare for the cross-examination of this expert report. That's a huge amount of work in itself, and it's time-consuming. So to prepare yourself - I'm not talking about the procedure or form - I'm talking about substance. At one point in time, I hope you've already started this, but you will have to pore over all the written statements of all witnesses, pore over all the documents and these are thousands and thousands of pages. So it's a huge amount of work. I believe that you need more than weeks, you need months to get ready. And giving you a few more months to get ready will prove, you know, to be very beneficial in the end. Notably, since I undertook - and I'm sure you've seen that so far I have lived up to my promises - I really undertook to meet with you at least every three weeks in order to look at all the problems. I believe that everything that can be solved upstream will be time saved downstream, if we can manage to solve a great number of problems before the trial in the pre-trial phase, then according to the spirit of the Statute and the text we will have a fair -- a quick trial. Not expeditious, not time-consuming, we will not waste time over procedural questions and so on, as we see so often because we will have been able to overcome all these problems in the pre-trial phase. I've prepared a working schedule where we meet every three weeks or so, and I'm sure we'll be able to save a lot of time in this pre-trial phase preparing for the trial. You told us, and I did hear you well, that the other Trial Chamber had planned to give Prosecution six months and to give you six months also. I believe that Prosecution could even be even quicker. I'll say how later on. Maybe we could save time on the presentation of the Prosecution's case, while of course allowing the Prosecution to present its evidence, but I think we could still save time. As you said yourself, you -- you believe that you will need six months for your own case. But you have to make sure that a lot of problems are ironed out earlier, otherwise we may run into difficulties. I think we should now have a break, a 20-minute break, and we'll resume after the break and you will have the floor. So you can give us your opinion on what was just said. It's now five to 5.00 and we will meet again around 5.15. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. The hearing is resumed. Mr. Seselj, regarding the issue of the date for the opening of trial, do you have anything to say on this?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] [Interpretation] The convention of human rights guarantees a minimal and fundamental right to all accused persons, namely trial within a reasonable period of time. The American and the African convention both agree on that. So what is a reasonable deadline within which a trial has to start for anyone accused of any crime, let alone the most serious of crimes, as in this case? In my view as far as my case is concerned - and I'm a record-holder in this Tribunal with regard to this matter - even if I had been provisionally released, the reasonable deadline for starting the trial is way behind us. In Serbia an accused person could spend a maximum of six months in detention prior to trial; in exceptional cases, one year. After the mafia coup of the 5th of October, the puppet regime, pro-Western, was brought into power and now the maximum pre-trial detention is two years. Judge, you were President of a court of appeals in Paris, if I have been informed correctly, and my friend Jacques Berger [phoen] considers you to be one of the top legal man in France. Would you please be kind to tell me what is the maximum amount of time that an accused person should spend in detention in a French prison? What is going on here is something that constitutes a very, very bad precedent. Detention that goes on for this long a period of time makes impossible a fair trial to begin with. Even if I were to have stayed in Belgrade this long, a fair trial would be impossible, let alone under these conditions. I understand all the things you said as to why the trial cannot start before November. I understand courtrooms that are overbooked and so on and so forth. However, there is one thing that remains inexplicable. Why did four and a half years have to go by until now? Why did the trial not start in 2003 within a reasonable amount of time? Carla del Ponte came to Belgrade in February 2003 when I came, and she said that everything was ready for my trial and that it could start immediately. It was the autumn of 2003 that was referred to. In 2004, I asked for provisional release until the beginning of the trial. It was rejected. One of the arguments - I don't want to go into all of them - was that the trial is expected to start in 2004, and of course, the trial did not start. In all fairness, an expanded indictment was issued, or rather, a request was submitted first of all. I did not oppose that because just like the previous charges were false, those charges were false, too. It's all the same to me, how many charges there will be, how many counts there will be, and how many crimes I will be charged with. You know, there is one thing that upsets me a bit and that is when lists of victims are read out and somebody who is not very well-versed in this may think that I am the person to be blamed for these victims, so I don't like the idea of that. However, I must say that I've had a good time, I've had quite a bit of fun over these years as I was watching all the trouble that the Prosecution was going through as they were trying to stage this trial and to see what they would do about this, which really made them sweat. Last year, the indictment was shortened, but it did not include everything that was added in 2005. But half of what I was charged with in 2003 was added, which shows that there is really a lack of seriousness in preparing this indictment. So this had nothing to do with expediting the proceedings, that is to say, decreasing the number of locations involved and the number of crimes involved, but the Prosecution realised that none of these crimes have anything to do with me. And the remaining ones don't have anything to do with me either. I got a list of witnesses only the other day, although the Trial Chamber said that all elements that have to do with the crime base in Western Slavonia should be eliminated, Samac, Bijeljina, Brcko, and so on. Yet again, witnesses are repeated on this list, there are about 106 of them, crime base witnesses, people who perhaps never saw me in their lives. Again this is some kind of a game they are playing; the Prosecution is not doing its job seriously. When they will start doing their job seriously, I have really lost all hope that they will ever do that. And that is what they attest to with their behaviour here and now. They are just trying to evade their responsibilities in terms of disclosure, they are rendering it impossible for me to resort to my procedural rights and so on and so forth. There were different ways of economising. In 2003, I was prepared to talk to the Prosecutor and I wanted to give them proof that many of these alleged crimes have nothing to do with the volunteers of the Serb Radical Party, so this was this key evidence that precluded any responsibility. Even if a volunteer of the Serb Radical Party had committed a crime somewhere, that would have had nothing to do with me; however, these are crimes that have nothing to do with any volunteers from the Serb Radical Party, as a matter of fact. The Prosecution gave me a list of questions and I put forth a requirement of my own that my legal advisors be present and the Prosecution just dodged that. And then the Trial Chamber, whose member you were too, instructed the OTP to do away with the crimes related to Vojvodina because in Vojvodina there was never an armed conflict. There is no nexus with the armed conflicts in other territories of the former Yugoslavia. In the case law that we see to date, I've read out -- I have read all the judgements and people had to prove that crimes were committed in a particular municipality, not a broader area. And also, there is no evidence that there were any attacks against the civilian population in Vojvodina; there were just some sporadic incidents but not a single one of them in terms of its intensity, social threat, and so on and so forth cannot measure up to Article 5 of the Statute. The Appeals Chamber, nevertheless, returned this with the explanation that these facts had to be proven through the trial. Why? In order to have a more extensive trial, to obtain certain political objectives through this trial, and in order to make the defence increasingly difficult, to give me a lot of work for my defence so that I cannot truly exercise my rights. The methods applied were aimed at making it difficult for me to conduct my defence. Now we are back to square one. My real preparations for my defence began only about three months ago, after I started communicating in a normal manner with my legal advisors, and of course once I recovered from the point of view of my health. And of course I have such a lot of evidence that I can refute each and every count. The Prosecutor needs a lot more time than I do. Of course I'm going to use the next six months in a useful manner, even a year, the question remains whether they will be trial-ready in November at all; however, the OTP is not using its time rationally. They did not display a good-will to do their job, to fulfil their commitments, because had they started doing their job properly three months ago I would have already achieved some results. They did not do what they were supposed to do during these three months, again, they did not redact or revise their lists properly, they still have these dead people on their witness list, and then also they want to introduce hundreds and hundreds of items of evidence and a few days ago they gave Terrence's [phoen] report - that is the expert report I referred to at the last conference when I told you that I didn't get this - and seven or eight pages are blacked out. Why? So that I would not disclose the names of witnesses? Not true. They are trying to disclose -- to hide some descriptions for no reason whatsoever, except to mistreat me. This expert report works to my benefit rather than their benefit. I can assure you of that. So how long will this go on? Until somebody from the OTP is called to account for not doing their job properly, not meeting their responsibilities to the Trial Chamber, to the accused, and to international justice at that. When you took over this case, Judge, you faced many motions for protective measures. Not one of these motions was explained properly, not in a single case did they prove that protective measures were really needed or did they prove that any witness was truly jeopardised. Also, you received several motions that some witnesses testify by videolink. The previous Trial Chamber readily agreed to that, but I ask you to review all of that because the fact that somebody is afraid to travel by plane is not an argument for letting them testify by videolink. If they're afraid to travel by plane, let them travel by bus, by train, let them hitch-hike, let them take a bicycle, but that is not an argument for testifying by videolink. If somebody has pneumonia, he must have recovered by now, what kind of pneumonia is that that can last for a year or whatever. Or if somebody has a headache or somebody is simply old. How can someone who is that old and cannot travel by plane can be a witness in a serious trial? No. For reasons of health such a person is no longer capable of testifying, so what we see here is a true obstruction of justice, abuse of legal proceedings. I refer you to the original doctrine related thereto. This is a magnificent case of that, what abuse of due process is. You could really teach law students what it is in this way. Of course, I'm going to wait for November. I'm going to wait for November of year as well, but as far as some questions are concerned, the Trial Chamber and you as the Pre-Trial Judge have to give me answers. What is a reasonable deadline for the beginning of trial and has it been overstepped? If it has, indeed, been overstepped, and I am convinced that that is the case, what are the consequences involved then? Why then have any proceedings, once the deadline for a reasonable process has elapsed? These are crucial questions that merit a proper answer. Once an answer is given to these questions, then we can deal with concrete details.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I am going to try and answer some of the points you raised to a certain extent. First, that issue of a reasonable time-period. You rightly point out that there is case law, including that by the European Court of Human Rights as to the issue of a reasonable period. Many countries have translated into their legislation the fact that if an accused had not been tried by a certain period he had, ex officio, to be released. The European Court of Human Rights condemned many states for failing to try individuals within a reasonable time-period. However, the same European Court of Human Rights added that the concept of reasonable time-period had to be assessed on a case-by-case basis. Sometimes certain factors, they said, had to be taken into account, certain constraints had to be taken into account. Regarding your personal case, as you know and you said so yourself, I was myself a Judge of Trial Chamber II. When I arrived here in this Tribunal in October of 2003, I was appointed as a member of Trial Chamber II. And I then discovered your existence. Until then, I did not know you at all, and I immediately noted that you had filed and were filing many motions. As a specialist of criminal law, I very quickly concluded that the number of motions you had filed was undoubtedly connected to the fact that your trial was not beginning, and since it had not begun you were going into procedural matters. I sought some information, I wanted to know how things were happening specifically in order to fix a time to open the trial. I was a Pre-Trial Judge in many cases, and I know it is up for the Pre-Trial Judge to seize the Trial Chamber, to say that case is trial-ready and that the trial should begin. But I also noted that there was, within this Tribunal, a coordinating committee with the President of the Tribunal, the Registrar, and the Chief Prosecutor, so as to ascertain depending on administrative, financial, budgetary constraints, work-load when a trial should start. In your case, I immediately realised that the main problems regarding your case were the fact that you wanted to represent yourself and, as you know, I did not agree with my colleagues. I had a dissenting opinion on one of your motions, setting out that you were entitled to represent yourself equally. Regarding disclosure of material, there was a debate within the Trial Chamber, and I had written a dissenting opinion, stating that you should have in hard copy your documents in your own language. It so happens that the Trial Chamber was then -- lost the case and it was given to another Trial Chamber so that I could not deliver my dissenting opinion. Thirdly, another major issue was the payment of your assistants. There again I told my colleagues that in my view if you represented yourself, you needed to be aided. So all the topics that have represented obstacles I had sort of noted them a long time ago. Why hasn't your trial started yet? As you know -- and you really pointed to the true reason. The true reason is that the Prosecutor is the one who decides when the case should go to trial. Why so? Because the Prosecutor discloses material to the accused whilst continuing investigations. Therefore, the Prosecutor will at a later stage introduce into evidence transcripts of current cases or parts of judgements or will ask for judicial notice of specific facts. Therefore, the Prosecutor has a strategy. In some countries, including in mine but it might be so too in your country, the Prosecutor is the one who chooses the dates for hearings. He has control over the dates. The Rules, our Rules, are silent on this. We have a tacit rule. We don't know exactly who makes the decision. Normally speaking, it is the trial -- the Pre-Trial Judge who must sort of close a chapter at that stage of the proceedings, say it's over; then the President should appoint the Bench and the Registrar will do everything necessary to get the case opened or the trial opened. In this issue, in this court, you are right; it is not normal that you should have been waiting trial several years. I can only agree with you in this. What has been the practice of this Tribunal? We must spell it out for it to be recorded in the transcript, because I told you I don't hide anything and as an independent judge, I express my opinion, which is as follows. When it comes to choosing dates for opening trials, there are a number of constraints, some of which I have now enumerated, but there's also the fact that the Prosecutor has a total control over disclosure of material and of the time when they say that they are trial-ready. Such conduct or control, however, is subjected to the control by the Trial Chamber and the Pre-Trial Judge. It so happens that the Rules under Rule 65 ter allowed for the pre-trial stage to be conducted initially by a Senior Legal Officer. And in several cases, the Judges were not the ones who were operating on the front line, as it were; it was the Senior Legal Officer who was in charge of preparing the case. They would meet with Defence counsel and the Prosecutor, and would inform the Pre-Trial Judge only later. This is the system that was in place until such time as President Meron appointed a committee presided over by Judge Bonomy and the committee made some suggestions, among which there was one saying that the Pre-Trial Judge had to be on the first line, on the front line, and personally I did not await the conclusions of the committee and its report in order to really devote my time to various cases as a Pre-Trial Judge. And I pressurised the OTP for them to get their case trial-ready. But the very fact that in some files, in some cases, which was also your case in the beginning, the Judges were not the ones in -- on the front line for the pre-trial stage, it was the Senior Legal Officer in charge of it. Secondly, in some cases, whilst the Statute was really quite clear on this when you had an indictment and when the accused was arrested, he was transferred to the Tribunal and he was to be tried quickly. That's what the Statute said. But it happened that the Tribunal started like with a cruising speed that was slower, and then little by little cases were tried one after the other, and this concatenation led to a bottle-neck. What happened then? In some cases, the accused could not be tried straight away; therefore, they applied for provisional release and were provisionally released. We have several cases that you are aware of as well as I am. They were released, provisionally so, and then the pre-trial stage was conducted whilst they were on provisional release; and then thereafter the cases were settled when there was a date for beginning the trial, the accused returned to The Hague and their trial began. You were not able to enjoy this regime inasmuch as you had been arrested while others came after you and were provisionally released. So somewhere you have now been detained for several years and this is a disturbing situation for more than one. This is the reason why in the decision on the contempt of court you haven't yet had the translation in your own language, but we say in this decision that you have been detained for several years, which goes to show that we are not indifferent to your situation. In this instance, there's no expedited procedure under the Rules. The Statute was very clear; trials should be expeditious and you should have been tried after a certain period of time. I, myself, made some suggestions in order to speed this up. I seized the Rules Committee of various proposals, unfortunately they were not followed through. I suggested, among other things, that from the time of the initial appearance to the date of trial opening, there should be, at best, six months which was more than enough. But this was not taken up. Therefore, the Rules do not solve this problem. And I can only, like you, be saddened and regret the situation. And as I said to you earlier on, for numerous reasons, and I'm going to mention one of them later on, the trial cannot start tomorrow. The reason I wanted to mention is the following. You filed a motion regarding the indictment, and you say that you should be entitled to raise a preliminary motion because you challenge the latest indictment. I have to remind you of a few things for it to be understood properly because this is a new problem that has just cropped up. Please take note, if you feel it necessary because everything is very accurate. The initial indictment contained 14 counts. It was written on the 15th of January, 2003. You, yourself, arrived in the Tribunal a few days later because you surrendered on the 24th of February, 2003. There was the initial appearance in which you pleaded not guilty. Regarding the indictment of the 15th of January, 2003, you filed a motion on the 24th of December, 2003, and on the 26th of May, 2004, Trial Chamber II, of which I was part, asked the Prosecution to specify the modes of liability held against you and in particular the Prosecution was to tell the Trial Chamber what they understood by the term "commit." On the 1st of November, 2004 - so it took the Prosecution some time to file an answer because the Trial Chamber had made that request on the 26th of May. On the 1st of November, 2004, so you were talking about grounds or reasons, this is one of them, the OTP filed a motion for leave to amend the initial indictment. It was amended whilst new geographical areas or bases were added. I'm going to quote them but you know them as well as I do: The Sarajevo area, Bijeljina, Mostar, Nevesinje and Brcko. Trial Chamber II granted the amended indictment and informed you of your right to raise preliminary motions on the amended indictment. The amended indictment was filed on the 15th of July, 2005. You did not waste any time because only a few weeks later, on the 29th of August, 2005, you filed a motion on the form of the amended indictment. And this is the point where we get into the system which accounted for several problems. On the 23rd of September, 2005, the Pre-Trial Judge issued a decision dismissing your 50-page motion on the ground that the said motion did not -- was not consistent with the Practice Direction, but there was a corollary to the decision. You were allowed to file a new motion by the 7th of October, 2005. On the 28th of September, 2005, you filed a motion on the issue of the length of the motion, but in your filings you had not spoken on the merits. On the 20th of October, 2005, you filed another motion for certification on appeal of the decision of the 23rd of September, 2005, and you also asked for an extension of the time-period for preliminary motions, explaining that you needed that time whilst awaiting the translation of some ICTR judgements in Serbian. On the 26th of October, 2005, Trial Chamber II dismissed your motion for certification, whereupon you filed another motion for certification, asking again for an extended time to file your preliminary motions. And I discover that apparently this new motion has remained unanswered. It got lost obviously. Then you were asked to plead to the amended indictment on the 3rd of October, 2005. I remember that because I then followed the Status Conference; you'd asked the registrar - not this deputy registrar - but to read out the entire indictment. I remember that well. And the Pre-Trial Judge asked you whether you would plead guilty or not guilty. You failed to answer, and the Judge thought that further to Rule 62(A), that you had pleaded not guilty. Out of this stage when you look at it, you realise that there were a lot of complications: That apparently one of your motions was not dealt with and also that some motions of yours for certification challenging the form of the indictment had been dismissed. Thereafter, there was - and I was the one who really advocated this - there was a new rule added to the Rules, Rule 73 bis (D). This has an advantage; it allows the Prosecutor to reduce the number of counts and to also fix a number of crime sites or incidents. Based on that, Trial Chamber III ordered the Prosecution to apply the provisions of Rule 73 bis. Therefore, the Prosecution removed Counts 2, 3, 5, 6, and 7 from the indictment. And the Trial Chamber indicated that the Prosecution would not be allowed to adduce evidence to crimes committed in Western Slavonia, Brcko, Bijeljina, Bosanski Samac, and Boracko Jezero but that the Prosecution would be allowed to adduce evidence which would not be crime based evidence for the same locations, which is in itself already a further complication. Based on that, there was an indictment that was issued on the 30th of March, 2007, a copy of which you received on the 17th of April, 2007. You, yourself, with the help of your legal advisors, you filed a motion to the Trial Chamber asking for leave to use the relevant rules so as to be able to challenge the indictment, the new indictment. So you filed a motion and the Prosecution will have to supply a response, will be settled, will be determined by the Trial Chamber. I alone cannot issue a decision because this motion is not within the scope of the Pre-Trial Judge alone. This is a jurisdiction of -- under the jurisdiction of the Trial Chamber, which is currently presided over by Judge Robinson, together with myself and Judge Bonomy. But I can tell you as far as your motion is concerned, whatever the response of the Prosecution may be and the attitude of my fellow Judges, I believe that you should be authorised to challenge the indictment, the new indictment. I don't know what the Trial Chamber is going to say, but as far as I am concerned I am very clear. Why so? Because I realised that in the previous proceedings there had already been a motion that had not been translated and it would be only logical that within the framework of the new indictment you should be given leave to challenge it, also because before you had this dispute with the assigned counsel and then you were not in a position to give any instructions to your Defence counsel, for them to possibly challenge the indictment. Therefore, I believe that you should be given leave to challenge the indictment. The Trial Chamber must determine the matter, that decision may again be challenged by you or the Prosecution, and the Appeals Chamber might be seized of it. In other words, this is one further element, a new factor, which leads me to say that it is impossible to start the trial because as I see it this would be prejudicial to your rights because you have the right to say that the indictment is not specific enough, is too vague, and you are entitled to challenge it. This is a right that was recognised to other accused, why not to you? And this is also something that I would say is an element that contributes to delaying the proceedings. The purpose of Rule 73 bis was to save time, and this shows that we're not gaining time or saving time. We're wasting time. We're trying to save time by reducing the counts of the indictment so you have to adduce less evidence, which means that you gain time on the length of the trial but you're wasting time because you open up a possibility for further delays inasmuch as you can challenge the indictment, the new indictment. So I had to take stock of the situation regarding this motion because it is very complicated. You really have to follow everything that happened on a day-to-day basis if you want to understand truly what the hurdles are. And I had to spell this out, because of course, the Prosecution will have to express their views on this, and I can only speak to my fellow Judges about this when I have heard all parties. And of course the point of view of the Prosecution can be possibly sort of replied to by Mr. Seselj; all this takes time, it is time-consuming. So, Mr. Seselj, do you want to say anything to this or do you believe that I really sort of gave a full overview of the situation regarding this motion?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Judge, I have one small addition. You have phrased this excellently. It was actually better than my own request. It is quite obvious that you are perfectly familiar with the heart of the matter, but I do have an additional explanation and this explanation has to do with a violation of my procedural rights back in 2005, when I was misled by the Trial Chamber in relation to the deadline for my filing an objection to the indictment. The amended indictment was filed on the 15th of July, I believe. This may not be perfectly accurate. I don't have the information in front of me. As soon as August, I think on the 22nd of August, I filed an objection. The objection had been put together before, but I was cut off for two months. I even had no phone lines to use to contact my family. In the Detention Unit, the administration of the Detention Unit, waited for that ban to be lifted, the ban on all my contacts with the outside world otherwise I would have filed the objection as early as July in all likelihood. One thing I didn't know was that the OTP were preparing supporting material for the amendments to the indictment. Nobody had informed me at the time that there was to be supporting material.
