According to the Rules, the deadline for objections starts on the day any supporting material to the indictment is submitted, and then by the end of that month. The Trial Chamber confirmed that I submitted my objection in a timely manner. This was then thrown out because of the fact that it contained too many pages, but then they did nothing to inform me that there would be further supporting material. I think this constitutes a serious violation of my procedural rights. I reacted once I had obtained the supporting material, but the Trial Chamber decided that I had missed my deadline -- or at least that was the conclusion that Judge Orie arrived at, and thus my request was thrown out. Why do I have the right to object to even an abbreviated of -- an abridged version of the indictment? Because the indictment was not abridged in a rational way; it was mechanically abridged and also in terms of its essence because the number of different counts and charges is now smaller. However, had a rational approach been taken, all the territories over which this International Criminal Tribunal has no jurisdiction would have been dropped such as Vojvodina where there was no armed conflict, for example. And there was nothing linking the clashes in Vojvodina to those in any other parts of the former Yugoslavia and primarily because there was no attack on the civilian population, on nothing that could be compared to the attacks mentioned in Article 5 of the Statute of the International Tribunal. These are three very powerful reasons for me to say that the indictment was not abridged in a proper way. A burden is left that will take up much of the OTP's time. They will have witnesses testifying here about a lot of unpleasant things that they probably experienced in their lives in an area where there were no expulsions, where people exchanged property, and had considerable profit, unlike most of the Serbs who had been driven out. Truth to tell, many of the refugees from Croatia and other republics of the former Yugoslavia came to Serbia. They flooded into Serbia, creating a lot of tension in Vojvodina. I was a politician, there was a pre-election campaign under way, and all I was saying is that our authorities should treat the Croat national minority the same way that Tudjman treated ours over in Croatia; however, our authorities never followed suit. There were no deportations and no expulsions. I wanted reciprocity, but this was not done. In this indictment they list a whole series of incidents, but in terms of sheer force or in terms of magnitude, none of them can be compared to those contained in Article 5 of the Statute. That's why I'm saying that the indictment was not abridged in a rational way. The OTP abridged the indictment based on political and not legal criteria because there is a political interest to stir things up about Vojvodina. Why? Because the American ambassador, the German ambassador in Belgrade says that Vojvodina is about to secede from Serbia, instead of having a systematic debate as to whether Croats were being politically threatened in Vojvodina or not. It is up to you to deal with this with the other Judges in the Trial Chamber but there is one other thing I wish to say. I never meant my objections to delay the start of this trial. Back in 2003 I raised an objection to the indictment in a timely manner, I think as early as April I can't remember exactly, but it was back in 2003. And then this was sent back to me because it contained too many pages and this was against the Rules. My basic procedural rights cannot be violated because of instructions by the Presiding Judge. Instructions are not binding. Instructions are not a binding norm. All right. The trial was meant to begin in the autumn of 2003. I had no intention of raising that objection again and putting it in writing, thinking that it might delay the start of trial. After all, it is my decision whether I would be objecting to the indictment or not. It was quite obvious in 2003 that the trial would not start and then I renewed my request at one of the Status Conferences. Judge Agius gave me new deadline for this objection and told me that I should keep it under or up to 50 pages, which is exactly what I did so I filed the objection. When in 2005 the indictment was amended I bore in mind that previous ruling, that I could file an objection of up to 50 pages. So I did just that again but this time around it was sent back again; it was thrown out and then all the new problems that came up, which is what forces me to re-open this issue now. Why? As an accused, I'm perfectly entitled to use every procedural error made by the OTP or any of the Judges for that matter. I have every intention of using that privilege but it is certainly not my intention to delay the start of trial. I will be adamant about this objection only if the trial really does not start in November. Why should I not be raising the objection? It's just another argument in my favour and I want to see how the Trial Chamber can come to grips with that. If the trial could start tomorrow, I would immediately give up all of my motions, all of my objections, with the exception of the criminal charges against Carla del Ponte and her associates because of the scandal involving false witnesses. I would do everything just for the trial to start as soon as possible. If I had all the time in the world -- there is a saying that our people use from back where I come from: The devil will find work for idle hands to do and that's what I do. I can distribute all the work to my legal assistants, but once I face a courtroom situation I will not have time to deal with procedural matters. But whenever I can use an error made by the Trial Chamber or the OTP to my advantage, I certainly will because I think that is something that definitely benefits me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Fine. For Prosecution, this was submission 287 of April 25, 2007. You must have received it. Did you reply, Mrs. Dahl, please?

utterances.speaker: MS. DAHL
utterances.text: Your Honour, our reply is due tomorrow and will be filed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Fine. So this was the first motion that I wanted to deal with. There is another motion, not give any names, but Prosecution filed a motion regarding Witness VS-031 pursuant to Rule 92 ter. The accused has replied, and Prosecution submitted its own reply. The Chamber can now rule, but I have a problem here. As I said earlier - and I will repeat - the Trial Chamber I belong to will not be the Trial Chamber that will try the case. So I wondered whether the pre-Trial Chamber must rule on motions that have to do with the substance of the proceedings; notably, the admissibility of a written statement under Article -- Rule 92 ter. Maybe it would be rather up to the Trial Chamber that will try the case to decide on the matter. Personally, I believe that a certain number of motions may wait for the Trial Chamber to actually decide on them. They're not jeopardising the accused as of now. Because in the end a decision will be made. I wanted this to be said. I'll give you the floor, Mr. Seselj, in a minute. Technically I could give an answer, simple and straightforward; however, maybe this would put my colleagues in front of a fait accompli because we will have made a decision, whereas they might have decided otherwise. Now, I will exactly explain this in a minute. 92 ter, Rule 92 ter works as follows. I am the source of this change in the Rules. The Rules were changed on September 13th, 2006, and since then a Trial Chamber can now admit as evidence a written statement in so far that the witness may be called up during the hearing and can be cross-examined by the accused and can answer questions from the Judges, from the Bench. This procedure helps save time. Experience has shown that most of the time viva voce witnesses are just repeating what they already stated in the written statement. We have this written statement. The Prosecutor is asking questions, the witness is answering and basically just repeating what he already said. So in some cases you can save time by admitting the written statement while of course allowing the accused to cross-examine the witness, because the accused must be here in the courtroom. Rule 92 ter can be fully understood if you keep in mind a triangle, and in this triangle you would have on the top angle viva voce witnesses who are examined by Prosecution and cross-examined by the accused, and you have other 92 ter witnesses which are talking about the same facts or the same events. But there, there's no need for examination-in-chief; there is, however, need for cross-examination. And then on the very third level, the lower level, is the 92 bis witness. These are witnesses that are only repeating what viva voce or 92 ter witnesses already stated. Let me give you an example to illustrate this. Let's imagine we have a viva voce witness saying that three cows were stolen from him; and a 92 ter witness would explain that his neighbour was a victim and that three cows were stolen from him; and in writing a 92 bis witness says that his neighbour saw three cows disappear. You don't need to have the three witnesses here in the courtroom to repeat the same thing. You just need to have one saying it, comforted, if need be, by a 92 ter and corroborated by a 92 bis. And in the end, everybody saves time, including the accused. Because when he brings his own witnesses he can also use this same pyramidal structure. And Witness VS-031 actually fits into this pattern, but this pattern must be accepted by the other Judges. I have my own opinion, but I don't know what the opinion of my colleagues is. If the Trial Chamber I belong to makes a decision right now, maybe the Judges that will sit in the Bench later, they might not agree with this decision, they might have another opinion. They say you did a lot of 92 ter where this should have been a viva voce witness. This is the dilemma. So, Mr. Seselj, you wanted to speak on this, I think.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Antonetti, I entirely agree that it is premature to rule on the admission of 92 bis witnesses or 92 ter witnesses as well as 92 quater, but there is an additional argument that I would like to raise. The OTP are adamant about this but they never told us who would be testifying to all these issues in court. So far we have witness VS-017, he was the first on the witness list and as an insider witness he was supposed to be the first to be heard at the December trial after the opening arguments of the OTP. He was the first person scheduled to testify as an insider witness. Now him being an insider no longer seems to matter; he'll just be rehashing certain things and we can introduce him as a 92 bis witness. That is what they are saying -- 92 ter witness. That is what they are saying now. Where is the legal logic behind this? Their most important witness is suddenly reduced to the status of an auxiliary witness, and we don't know who will be taking up the vacant spot of an insider witness. There is nothing on that list, there's nobody who will testify about all these issues that were foreseen for VS-017. So what is the whole thing about? I'll tell you what this is about. The former 92 bis rule is now subdivided into a 92 ter and 92 quater. The OTP and their investigators now draft a statement. They believe the witness to not be sufficiently educated, literate, or capable in order to give his own account in open court. The witness is brought in merely to confirm that the statement is authentic and belongs to him, often without understanding the statement. As I said at the Milosevic trial, there were over 40 cases of such witnesses stating this in court: This is not my statement. It was misinterpreted. They misheard what I said. I remember that. There were over 40 such cases in the Milosevic trial. There were things like that happening in other trials, too, but what I've been reading with particular interest is the Milosevic transcripts because they were published in this journal in Serbia, this free-thinking "Serbian Thought." So that's why I'd like them to bring all their witnesses here to testify in open court and then to explain in relation to all of their 92 ter and 92 quater witnesses why they did not appear live, and then there can be additional explanations which of the evidence would be detrimental to the accused under 92 ter and under 92 quater. The OTP are deliberately acting in a chaotic manner. They keep submitting new motions, new requests, but they have so far failed to bring order to their witness list to begin with, which is something that you ordered them to do at the first or second Status Conference, Judge, to say which witnesses would be testifying in open court and then all the other witnesses under 92 bis, 92 ter, and 92 quater. I will be opposing all of these because I think the only testimony that counts is testimony given in open court, but I'm powerless in the position that I'm in now and I cannot do that. I do, however, believe that the meaning behind the 92 bis, 92 ter, and 92 quater Rules is that they should be applied in exceptional circumstances only. However, exceptional has now become regular for the OTP. There is a danger that we shall see many more witnesses under these three additional rules as opposed to witnesses testifying in open court. At one point during the Milosevic trial, Geoffrey Nice said what they had come up with was 92 bis and a half which I suspect was later transformed into 92 ter. That is how much they wanted to get as much evidence as possible under 92 bis, the old 92 bis, and I think this OTP team is acting in much the same manner. And then they awarded Mr. Milosevic no more than 45 minutes or perhaps up to one hour, rarely more, for the cross-examination of all these witnesses. They tried to stop him every possible way from challenging the credibility of the witness, challenging the witness's facts. Now we see much the same thing at work as far as the OTP is concerned. That is why I support your position that all decisions on 92 bis, 92 ter, and 92 quater admissions should be made once the trial is underway and not before and once we have complete witness lists and a complete overview as to which witnesses shall be appearing in open court and which witnesses shall be 92 bis witnesses. And then we can have additional statements admitted under 92 bis, 92 ter, and 92 quater, all witnesses from other trials. As far as evidence given in other trials is concerned, it is impossible to take anything for granted before the OTP bring me the entire transcript. For example, they wanted Deronjic to appear as a witness in my case, although my indictment has nothing whatsoever to do with Bratunac. They wanted Milan Babic to appear in this trial; he was to be their crown witness and they tried to use him to tender most of their documents. There are those two and another four of the witnesses who are now deceased and they are now trying to tender their statements into evidence under 92 quater, although so far they have failed to submit their evidence from other trials in which these persons appeared. Get a typist, tell them to listen to all the tapes, and tell them to put it all down on paper in Serbian, the whole thing, then you can submit it to me and only then can I say whether I accept that or not, certainly not before such documents have been served on me. We can't have a serious discussion before you do this and this is no mean feat. I'm sorry you have so much on your plate, but maybe you can do something to circumvent all these complications. Why did you decide to try a person like this? Maybe you didn't know who you were dealing with, maybe you jumped the gun. I hope that now you understand who it is that you are dealing with.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] [Previous translation continues]... You mentioned Witness 31, Mr. Seselj. You also talked about Witness 17, well, independently of the numbers and of course, we will mention their names. I now turn to the Prosecution. You heard Mr. Seselj, I think I said the same thing as he did and we will look into this later on. However, I was looking at the document that you prepared regarding the schedule of witness, crime base for Vocin, for example, there were a number of witnesses that had been scheduled or planned. To make sure that we have a speedy trial and useful trial, I intend to ask Prosecution locality -- for each location to provide us with a chart in this triangular shape, this pyramidal shape. What witnesses are planned to be called as viva voce, as 92 ter, 92 ter.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction: Viva voce, 92 ter and 92 bis.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In order for us to see exactly what the pattern will be. If we have a witness scheduled as a viva voce turns into a 92 ter, there might be a reason for this. But here again and Mr. Seselj stated it but I also mentioned it, in this pyramidal pattern, you need to have a lead witness, a viva voce witness, that will be speaking and that will be answering the in-chief. We can't be in a system where we have a location where crime base events happened, we have no viva voce witness. And we just have a 92 bis, for example, or possibly a 92 ter, this can't be. So for each location, each area, you have to identify what witnesses will be viva voce witnesses, then of course the accused can prepare his cross-examination at best. You need also to indicate on the schedule what witnesses will be 92 ter and what witnesses will be 92 bis. The accused is entitled to a right, a right that is provided in the Statute, he has the right to cross-examine. This is an absolute right. So this right to cross-examination must be understood as follows, you know, I'm going back to my example of the three cows. You've got to cross-examine the witness that has stated that the three cows were stolen but he's got the right to cross-examine the other witnesses but he's going to waste time, of course, if he's asking the same questions to another witness, which is why, as soon as possible, the accused must have the schedule of witness with the nature of the witnesses, whether they're viva voce, 92 ter, 92 bis, possibly 92 quater. I'll come back to that later. So, Mrs. Dahl, do you need to take the floor? Is it still too early? I fully understand that it might be too early for you.

utterances.speaker: MS. DAHL
utterances.text: I'm not sure, Your Honour, what the question pending is. We have indicated through our submissions our intention to call witnesses in various modalities. Those questions are pending for resolution before the Trial Chamber, and I appreciate the Court's concern regarding important decisions made pre-trial that may influence or affect how the trial is conducted before the ultimate fact-finders. Having said that, I want to return briefly to the Court's comments earlier in recapitulating our position regarding trial-readiness and mention of a November trial date. It is not correct that the Prosecution is unable to prepare and start trial before November. When I mentioned the November trial date at the earlier Status Conference, we were trial-ready a year ago last fall, we are trial-ready now, and my indication regarding the November 2000 [sic] trial date was to ensure that Mr. Seselj had adequate time to prepare. We must not jeopardise the fairness of the proceedings by short-changing his ability to make careful study of the material that has been tendered to him. We have discharged our disclosure obligations in this matter. He has elected to reject the materials that we have prepared and tendered to him, thus depriving himself of the ability to review the materials in detail. We consider on the matter of witnesses that this is a grave decision because we are not dealing with a matter of stolen cows. The case concerns stolen lives, and so we must be careful in our efficiency --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mrs. Dahl, I talked about cows because I did not want to talk about substance, which is why I used this example. Because of course the substance is for trial. I'm here for the preparation of the trial, to make sure that the preparation is at best, which is why I did not want to go into substance which is why I talked about cows. I could have talked about stolen cars, chicken, whatever. It was just an example, an illustration. So please don't go into all these kind of declarations.

utterances.speaker: MS. DAHL
utterances.text: In the consideration of the presentation of evidence and the need to ensure expeditiousness at trial, the Prosecution wants the best opportunity to present its evidence persuasively in a manner that allows fair consideration of the testimony of witnesses as well as adequate opportunity for cross-examination. So we consider the matter most appropriately resolved in time to allow the Prosecution to respond to the needs of the Chamber and to prepare the witnesses for the form that is ultimately decided upon to present the case and move the trial along quickly. We cannot have a quick trial at the -- and sacrifice thoroughness, and your submissions to date regarding the form of witness testimony have shown our willingness to adapt to the Rules of the Tribunal and to attempt to present the case in a way that facilitates fair finding of fact as well as adequate cross-examination to test the veracity of the statements by the witness. So we would appreciate guidance from the Trial Chamber in the terms of ruling on the pending motions so that we can meet our obligations in a timely manner.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I say something?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. Seselj.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] A few moments ago, Judge, as you were looking through this list of Prosecution witnesses, you mentioned that there were a few witnesses who testified about the crime base in Vocin. Vocin is in Western Slavonia. Western Slavonia is out of the indictment now. How come these witnesses appear now on the witness list? Again, they have not been excluded. So now have they been excluded or not? This Vocin is no longer in the indictment. And I still have a few witnesses, crime base, testifying about Vocin. Am I supposed to prepare for their testimony or not? Why have they not been excluded from this witness list? The Prosecution refuses to answer. Also some other sites that were excluded from the indictment are still mentioned. Ms. Dahl said a few moments ago that they stand trial-ready but she says it's my fault because I refused to receive some documents that they tried to disclose to me. What you have here is a very nice review that the Prosecution made on the 8th of November, 2006, and you can see on it exactly what I received, what I did not receive, and why I did not receive it. I did not receive it only because it was on computer CDs. I did not receive it only because it was in the English language or it was not disclosed to me at all, but rather to the imposed counsel, Hooper. This is the best proof of the Prosecution's guilt for the fact that the trial has not started yet. This does not work in favour of the Prosecution; it works against the Prosecution and they made it themselves. This is why the trial hasn't started yet, because over 300.000 pages of documents they have to submit to me. Not taking into account the new things like testimonies in different trials, statements of dead witnesses, and so on and so forth. Also not taking into account their old obligation to submit to me all testimonies from this institution that mention my name. This is an old obligation from 2003 or 2004, but they haven't honoured it yet. They haven't done it yet. How can they be trial-ready? Of course they are prepared to start the trial against me tomorrow but only if they not only tie my hands but also shut my mouth. If they could do that, then they would be trial-ready. Now when I can defend myself, they cannot carry out the trial. They say that I refused to accept certain things. It is your duty to give me everything on paper and in the Serbian language, and you have to do this even if I wait for another four years. There will be no trial without that, and you hesitate because you think that something will happen in that field. Nothing will happen. You will either do that or there will be no trial. There is no third option.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. I'm turning to the Prosecution regarding the witness list, the updated list, did you disclose to Mr. Seselj the latest, the updated list as you say in English, which takes stock of the situation as far as the witnesses are concerned, the witnesses you would call if the trial were to start tomorrow, of course taking into account the changes made to the indictment.

utterances.speaker: MS. DAHL
utterances.text: If I may, Your Honour, check with our case manager regarding the status of the translation of the witness list.

utterances.speaker: MS. DAHL
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm informed that we served on the accused in translation a witness list that reflected the latest modifications as of March 29, 2007.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. In my binder --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just wait a minute. I'm going to give you the floor, Mr. Seselj. I just want you to understand. On the 30th of March, 2007, the Prosecutor served the indictment -- the amended indictment and there are schedules attached to it, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, you've received it all. In Schedule A, you have the final list of witnesses, revised list, final revised list. But looking at this document it looks as if there were going to be 105 witnesses. You mentioned Vocin earlier on, saying it was in Slavonia and that you didn't understand why there would still be witnesses under the Vocin category. But I'm looking at the list and I see that, indeed, there are witnesses who are scheduled. I see witness numbers, I'm not going to give the names, Witness 18, Witness 33, Witness 50, and others with names. So there is a given amount of witnesses for the said municipality -- or for that one there's one witness, two, three, four, five, six -- yeah, six witnesses for that municipality. There it is. In theory, you should have had the witness list. Was it translated? I don't know, but in principle you should have it. Yes, Mr. Seselj.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I have received that list and that is what I am talking about, Judge. You have already mentioned six crime-based witnesses related to Vocin, Western Slavonia, but then you also have witnesses testifying about the crime base in Bijeljina, Brcko, Samac, and all of that has been excluded from the indictment. I just remember now a certain Alija Busalic who is not a protected witness, who started the war in Bijeljina, he's there on that list as a crime base witness from Bijeljina. It's not that I care about getting rid of this Alija Busalic, I would be more than happy to cross-examine him here, but you are violating my procedural rights because you are still keeping on the list crime-based witnesses from localities that have been taken out of the indictment. So, Judge, if you found six from Vocin, multiply that by four and then you will see how many such witnesses there are. I'm just speaking in very approximate terms now, I am not being precise enough, but I am referring to the core of the matter, not details. You have an enormous number of witnesses who are testifying about the crime base from localities that were completely excluded from the indictment. What can I do about that?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Ms. Dahl, Mr. Seselj has just raised a problem. He notices, but of course, subject to more thorough examination which I haven't carried out, it looks as though there were in the list witnesses regarding localities that have been stricken.

utterances.speaker: MS. DAHL
utterances.text: Your Honour, the decision of 8 November 2006 applying Rule 73 bis to the indictment permitted the Prosecution to lead pattern evidence regarding the crimes alleged in the indictment. We have substantially narrowed the witness list in response to the removal of certain crimes and counts from the indictment, but are exercising the prerogative afforded us in the Trial Chamber's reduction of the indictment to lead pattern evidence. We have endeavoured to narrow it and will continue in reflecting on the witness list and the type of evidence to be led to make the modifications that are appropriate without impairing the case. It will assist us to know the Trial Chamber's rulings on the form of evidence in the motions that are pending decision. That will help us to assess the necessity of witnesses, the overlaps, or as the Court indicated their position in the pyramid. Our witness list presently indicates the form of testimony and the relevance with regard to the charged allegations. If Mr. Seselj considers that the witnesses that remain are excessive in number or will not prove pattern evidence or is willing to stipulate to the crime bases themselves and will agree to adjudicated facts that have been tendered to the Court by motion, we can eliminate and narrow the conflicts to be resolved at trial through the presentation of evidence. He can bring a motion, if he alleges that we have an excessive amount of proof that's in conflict with the decision of last November; but the reduction of the indictment must not carry with it the disablement of the Prosecution to prepare and prove its case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Ms. Dahl, I'm trying to understand. And I can reassure you, I have not looked at the file -- to the substance of the file, but from what I understand, the merit of Rule 73 bis is that it reduces. There were many municipalities in the indictment, and from what I understood now Slavonia is taken out of the scope of the indictment. But the Prosecution changed the indictment accordingly while leaving witnesses from the said municipality in order - and I take up your own words - to show a pattern, pattern evidence, that is, the scope and the repetition and so on and so forth. Is this how I should understand you? But what you prove in relation to other municipalities, do you, so you're going to pile up municipalities or localities, some of which has been taken out of the indictment and for which the accused will not have to be held innocent or guilty, but you will have witnesses from those municipalities who are going to say what happened to them happened elsewhere. Is that your approach?

utterances.speaker: MS. DAHL
utterances.text: When municipalities such as Vocin were removed, we eliminated 26 witnesses from the witness list. In consideration, now we have only six witnesses who will testify as to the pattern of the crimes that they were subjected to.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I say something, Judge?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. Seselj.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I'm astonished by this lack of professionalism on the OTP's side. If we're talking about pattern evidence, that can only be a pattern of my incriminated behaviour or criminal conduct, then there has to be evidence about what I did, not testimonies of witnesses who say that something unpleasant happened to them somewhere and then some of them never even saw me but just heard that I was somewhere out there in the area. What kind of a pattern is that? Pattern of crimes throughout the war? Well, then you could have brought in victims from the Muslim and Croat sides and they could have talked about an identical pattern, sometimes even worse. Whose pattern of behaviour? It has to be a pattern of my conduct in order to support the direct allegations from the indictment. So I am guilty because somebody killed such and such a number of people in Zvornik or in Vukovar and there is this kind of a pattern in other cases, too. You're not making an effort to prove that at all. If you look at this more carefully, the witness list, you will see that many of these witnesses do not directly charge me with anything. They just talk directly about their own tragic war experience, provided it is true; there are some witnesses who talk about things that are not true. So even there the OTP did not observe the decision of the Trial Chamber. I repeat yet again, I would be the happiest if you were to allege that I committed all the crimes committed in this war and to have the trial go on for 20 years and that I eliminate each and every one of your charges and then in this way I emerge victorious from all of this 20 years later and then I would know why I was born. What I'm indicating to you now is a violation of the ruling of the Trial Chamber, you're violating procedure. We're not talking about a pattern of conduct of all sorts of criminals in this war; we are just talking about a pattern of my own conduct as a specific individual who you proclaim to be a criminal in advance and you simply cannot prove that at all. And I am growing old and grey here and you are not capable of proving that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I will look into this in a more specific way later. But, Mrs. Dahl, you weren't there yet but I told Mr. Saxon who was there that the indictment was like a three-stage rocket. I'm quoting from memory because I don't have the transcript of my own words, but out of memory I had explained that the first stage of the rocket were the victims who were coming here to say what had happened. That's crime base, and this involved a certain number of municipalities. If some municipalities or villages were stricken out, then there's no longer any need to have these witnesses here. Now, second stage of the rocket - and I mean this is the normal way to proceed when you're dealing with legal matters - who committed the crime. And there you need evidence to prove that it is Mr. X, Mr. Y who actually committed the crime, destruction, looting, and so forth and so on. That's the second stage. And this is the approach that must be adopted by Prosecution. Now, the third stage, it's the accused. We need to know the connection to the crimes committed, maybe through those who actually committed the crimes. And in such case, you need to prove the connection between the crime, the perpetrator, and the accused, if the accused did not personally commit the crime. I'm setting aside the JCE which is a mode of liability under Article 7(1), but JCE also must be proved, of course. I had asked your predecessor, Mr. Saxon, how he intended to adduce his evidence according to these three main stages. Now he's gone, you've replaced him, and I'm asking you the same question. Because for the Bench as well as for the accused, this is going to be very important because it helps you adopt a certain procedure and save time. Out -- in several cases, out of experience, I've seen that sometimes we have witnesses coming, everything is mixed up. So I fully understand that Prosecution doesn't fully control who can come at what time and so on. But very logically we would need to have all witnesses from a specific municipality and then hear other witnesses from another municipality and not jump from one witness to the other from one municipality to the other and so on, because then it's a waste of time. Then once evidence has been adduced and then the crimes -- it is proved that crimes have been committed then you need to know who committed the crime and there you need additional evidence. Then you need to have those witnesses that are going to make the connection between the accused and the actual perpetrators. A criminal trial has to follow a specific structure and a specific logic. Prosecution must absolutely prove, Prosecution has the burden of proof. The accused could almost just stay still and wait for the proof to be given, but the accused here can cross-examine. But if he's to cross-examine he must have all the necessary elements at his disposal which is why we have these Status Conferences that help move forward and really understand what problems lie ahead. Unfortunately, we're going to have to sum up, it's already 7.00 p.m., but we will soon meet again. In the meanwhile, I will have ruled on the disclosure in hard copy and in the accused's language of all the documents, including those who were in those 40 binders, those notorious binders. So theoretically, very quickly, the accused will have at his disposal all the evidence which will be - I say will - will be used during trial. I mean the documents that will be presented to the witness, the witnesses that we'll be hearing. That's the minimum that the accused must have at his disposal. And this is a hurdle that I must absolutely overcome as quickly as possible. Second hurdle, I mentioned it, it's the financial resources provided to the accused. I'm waiting for his motion. I'm sure he'll be very hasty in doing this. And in this regard I would like to tell Mr. Seselj that on January 3rd, 2006, you made a submission, 104, submission 104 --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: 124, Interpreter's correction.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 124, exactly on this topic so you could go back to this submission, submission 124, to back the new motion that you must file. Now, given the 15-day deadline, maybe when we meet again on June 5th, I will, I'm not sure, but I might have already ruled on this. I've already started to look into this. As soon as I have the position of Prosecution, I will be able to make my ruling and then the second hurdle will be overcome. Now, the third hurdle, it's the problem of the indictment. Here again I'm waiting for a reply from Prosecution. I will, of course, talk about this to my colleagues because we need to make a decision here as a Bench. During the next pre-trial -- next Status Conference, I'm sure we'll be able to go back to some of these topics and I hope that they will have advanced correctly and positively. Those who seem to be stuck in a quagmire, I'll do my best to try and move them forward. And as we come closer to the opening of the trial, we will look at the way the Prosecution will adduce its evidence. I think I understood Mrs. Dahl that you are waiting for some guidance from us, and we will provide you with guidance on this. But now it's 7.00 p.m. I'm sorry that I was so lengthy, and we will meet again very soon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: adjourned at 7.03 p.m.
